clean_description: The Boys in the Boat tells the true story of the University of Washington's eight-oar crew team, composed of working-class boys, who triumphed at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin. Led by Joe Rantz, who faced personal hardships, the team defied expectations by defeating elite crews from the East Coast and Great Britain, culminating in a historic victory against the German team. The narrative explores themes of perseverance, camaraderie, and the impact of the Great Depression on their lives.
